answer: A harbor that admits any ship without inspection soon fills with fake hulls, so an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it can trade. The stake is a bridge between a cheap pseudonym and a costly commitment: a Sybil operator who wants a thousand identities must lock a thousand stakes, and misbehavior burns one. Honest agents pay nothing but the opportunity cost of locked funds, while the ripple of one slashed stake discourages the next thousand fakes.
